title.en: Retrying a start with the same Idempotency-Key never starts a second pot

goal.en: Networks drop answers. An agent that retries POST /v1/executions with the same Idempotency-Key gets the execution already started, in its current state, instead of a second run of the same recipe.

note.en: Start a shakshuka run with the key ex-044-idem-key.
The run advances to the first step that needs a person.
Send the identical request with the identical key, as a client would after a lost answer. The hub returns the same execution at its current state, not a new one.
Reading the status confirms there is one execution and it is the one both answers described.
The retry carried the plan of the original start.

cli: jq '. + {"x-hub-human-present": true}' examples/core/execute-request.json | curl -s -X POST http://localhost:7878/v1/executions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Idempotency-Key: ex-2026-10-04-001-a' -d @-

jq '. + {"x-hub-human-present": true}' examples/core/execute-request.json | curl -s -X POST http://localhost:7878/v1/executions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Idempotency-Key: ex-2026-10-04-001-a' -d @-

outcome.en: You can retry a start safely. Next: scenario 050 shows what happens when the key differs but the execution id repeats.
